REPORT DATE: 09-08-2021 REPORT TIME: 0520 UTC REGION: GULF OF MEXICO SUB REGION: N/A AREA/BLOCK: WEST DELTA 31 IMAGE DATE: 09-07-2021 IMAGE TIME: 2359 UTC DATA SOURCE: RADARSAT2 MODE: SCANSAR NARROW VV RESOLUTION: 50 METER LOCATION: 29°07"14" N/89°39"02" W AREA: 4.98 SQUARE KILOMETERS CONFIDENCE: HIGH REMARKS: POSSIBLE OIL WAS OBSERVED IN SATELLITE IMAGERY. THIS ANOMALY IS UNCONFIRMED AS OIL. THE BROKEN ANOMALY EXTENDED ABOUT 12 NM IN LENGTH BY APPROXIMATELY 0.2 NM IN WIDTH AT IT WIDEST POINT, HAD GOOD CONTRAST WITH ITS BACKGROUND AND HAD UNNATURAL TWISTS AND TURNS. ADDITIONALLY, THE ANOMALY APPEARED TO EMANATE FROM A POINT-SOURCE. WINDS WERE OUT OF THE SE AT 5 KT AT THE TIME OF THE IMAGE. THIS ANOMALY MAY BE RELATED TO ADDITIONAL MPSR"S GENERATED IN THE REGION OVER THE PAST SEVERAL DAYS. CONSIDERING THE ABOVE FACTORS, WE HAVE HIGH CONFIDENCE IN THIS ASSESSMENT. UNCERTAINTIES: NONE

properties.title: NRC Report: Shell Tellus 68 Hydraulic Oil in Tumon Bay near Tumon, GU
properties.summary: Incident Type: MOBILE - NRC Report ID: 891514 - Medium Affected: WATER - Suspected Responsible Party: LANDSCAPE MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS, INC.
properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 891514
Incident Time: 2008-11-22 14:30:00
Nearest City: Tumon, GU
Incident Type: MOBILE
Material: SHELL TELLUS 68 HYDRAULIC OIL
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: LANDSCAPE MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS, INC.
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 0.25 gallons
ON SATURDAY, NOV. 22, 2008 JERRY TOMAS WAS OPERATING A KUBOTA TRACTOR TO CLEAN UP THE TRASH ALONG YPAO BEACH BELOW THE PACIFIC ISLANDS CLUB. AT 9:30 AM THE HYDRAULIC HOSE FOR THE POWER STEERING CYLINDER BROKE RELEASING HYDRAULIC OIL. AT 9:35 JERRY CALLED OUR MECHANIC TEODORO VENTURA TO ADDRESS THE PROBLEM. AT 10:30 A.M. TEODORO ARRIVED AT THE SITE AND REMOVED THE HOSE TO FIND A REPLACEMENT. HE ALSO WRAPPED THE AREA WITH CLOTH, APPLIED ABSORBENT PADS UNDERNEATH AS WELL AS A PAN TO CATCH THE LEAKING HYDRAULIC OIL. HE AND JERRY LEFT THE SITE TO FIND THE REPLACEMENT HOSE. AT 12:00 PM THEY RETURNED TO THE BEACH SITE. AT THIS TIME THEY NOTICED THAT THE TIDE WAS COMING IN. AT 12:15 P.M. THEY LEFT THE BEACH SITE AND CAME TO THE TUMON OFFICE TO FIND A REPLACEMENT HOSE. AT 3:00 PM JERRY SPOKE TO BOB SALAS, WHO IN TURN CALLED OUR HEAD MECHANIC PAT FEJERAN. PAT ARRIVED AT THE TUMON OFFICE AT APPROXIMATELY 3:27 P.M., THEN HE, JERRY AND TEODORO WENT BACK DOWN TO THE BEACH SITE AND PAT ASSESSED THE PROBLEM. AT 3:30 HE LEFT THE BEACH SITE TO FIND A REPLACEMENT HOSE. HE WENT TO THE COCKPIT TO SEE IF HE COULD TAKE A HOSE FROM ONE OF THE OTHER MACHINES. HE WAS ABLE TO CUT A COMPATIBLE HOSE FROM THE JOHN DEERE MOWER AND CUT TWO FITTINGS TO USE FOR THE REPAIR. HE ALSO AT 6:15 LMS ARRIVED BACK AT THE BEACH SITE AND TEMPORARILY FIXED THE HOSE. BETWEEN 5:30 – 6:00 PM GUAM EPA ARRIVED ON THE SCENE. AT 6:20 PM, THE TRACTOR WAS REMOVED FROM THE BEACH.

Report Description
CALLER IS REPORTING A RELEASE OF SEAWATER THAT WAS DISCHARGED FROM THE BILGE ON A NAVY VESSEL. CALLER STATED THIS WAS DONE TO PREVENT THE VESSEL FROM FLOODING IN THE JAMES RIVER IN NEWPORT NEWS, VIRGINIA. THIS CAUSE OF THE DISCHARGE INCIDENT: CALLER STATED DUE TO AN OPERATOR ERROR THERE WAS A DISCHARGE OF SEAWATER. WHILE DOING MAINTENANCE ON A VALVE ON THE MAIN CONDENSER ON THE VESSEL ANOTHER VALVE ASSOCIATED WITH THE SYSTEM WAS SOMEHOW INADVERTENTLY OPENED BY ACCIDENT. THIS CAUSED WATER TO INGRESS INTO THE MAIN CONDENSER ALLOWING THE CONDENSER TO OVERFLOW INTO THE ENGINE ROOM BILGE. CALLER STATED AT THE TIME SOURCE WAS UNKNOWN. FOR THE SAFETY OF THE VESSEL AND CREW THEY ACTIVATED SUBMERSIBLE PUMPS TO PUMP THE WATER OVER THE SIDE OF THE VESSEL.
